open_points.subject: A13 owner-session concurrency
open_points.text: “a request that passes it completes even if a limit passes while it runs” covers time limits, but says nothing about a concurrent sign-out or instance restart
open_points.question: Does an in-flight owner request that already passed session validation complete if the session is signed out or the instance begins restarting before it commits?
options: It completes once validation has passed
Sign-out or restart cancels/refuses it
Sign-out cancels it but passage of a restart boundary is impossible because shutdown waits
open_points.default_guess: Let a request that passed validation complete; serialize sign-out behind it and use graceful shutdown.

open_points.subject: A13 simultaneous owner sessions
open_points.text: “The owner signs in ... and receives an owner session” does not say what a later successful sign-in does to existing owner sessions
open_points.question: May several owner sessions coexist, or does a successful sign-in invalidate an earlier one?
options: Allow multiple independent sessions
Invalidate all earlier sessions
Invalidate only an earlier session from the same browser
open_points.default_guess: Allow multiple independent sessions until each reaches its own end condition.

open_points.subject: A13 session-cookie policy
open_points.text: The cookie is only specified as “scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact Secure, SameSite, Domain and Path policy applies, especially when Registry is reached locally without HTTPS?
options: Host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, with Secure whenever HTTPS is used
Always require HTTPS and always set Secure
Permit a non-Secure host-only cookie on local HTTP and use SameSite=Lax
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, Path=/, and require Secure outside local HTTP.

open_points.subject: A13 expiry and retained session data
open_points.text: “The session ends” at its time limits and “Everything in it ends with the session,” but no rule says whether expiry is actively processed or discovered only on the next request
open_points.question: When must an expired session and its uploaded personal-data import file be removed if no later request presents that session?
options: Remove them at the expiry instant with scheduled cleanup
Mark/remove them lazily when next observed
Keep expired runtime objects until periodic cleanup or restart
open_points.default_guess: Schedule cleanup so the session and uploaded file are removed at expiry.

open_points.subject: A15 audit sequence after restore
open_points.text: A15 says sequence numbers are “never reused in a store” and its invariant says every later-written entry has a greater number, while A18 says restoration continues from the backup's last number after later entries have been lost
open_points.question: May post-restore entries reuse sequence numbers that production wrote after the restored backup, or must a high-water mark survive outside the restored store?
options: Reuse is allowed because restoration starts a new store history
Keep an external high-water mark and never reuse a number across restore
Give the restored store a new lineage identifier so sequence numbers are unique only within a lineage
open_points.default_guess: Treat restoration as a new store lineage and permit reuse, while making the invariant explicitly lineage-scoped.

open_points.subject: A16 imported object mapping
open_points.text: The mapping lists ids, status, rooms, pointers, names, aliases and Customers, but does not say that it shows the embedded object's address, kind and characteristics, although the import must carry the object inside its project
open_points.question: Are the imported object's values shown to the owner in the mapping, and exactly which of them are imported or editable there?
options: Show and import every object value from the file unchanged
Show all object values and allow the owner to replace them in the mapping
Import them without showing them
open_points.default_guess: Show every object value and import it unchanged.

open_points.subject: A16 empty project selection
open_points.text: The owner may pick projects and the accepted transaction stores “every picked project,” but the rules never say whether an empty set of picks is valid
open_points.question: Can confirming an import with no selected projects create the migration closure and permanently close the one import?
options: Refuse an empty selection
Accept it and close the import
Allow an empty preview but require at least one pick at confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Refuse confirmation unless at least one project is selected.

open_points.subject: A16 imported display names
open_points.text: A16 defaults each project to “its v1 name and no alias unless the owner gives others,” while R0-82 says projects imported under a person's name are renamed and R0-85 says the import is the one moment an archived project's name is set
open_points.question: When may the v1 display name be retained, and how is the required renaming of a person-named project enforced or confirmed?
options: Always require the owner to enter a new display name for every imported project
Allow the v1 name unless the owner identifies it as a person's name
Always retain the v1 name unless the owner voluntarily replaces it
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to confirm or replace every imported display name, without attempting automated name detection.

open_points.subject: A16 crash before the post-import backup
open_points.text: “Right after an accepted import Registry makes a backup run” does not say what happens if Registry stops after committing the import but before starting or completing that run
open_points.question: How does Registry detect and resume the required post-import backup after a crash or restart?
options: On every service-enabled start, compare the closure with checked backups and run one if none contains it
Wait for the next daily run
Persist a separate pending-post-import-backup flag in the import transaction
open_points.default_guess: On start, inspect the closure and checked backups and immediately run a backup if none contains the closure.

open_points.subject: A16 request-id collision disclosure
open_points.text: A01 says a differing request-id collision is refused and “the caller reads the record,” while A10 says Kernel never reaches a project outside its session's set; request ids are globally unique per model rather than scoped to a session or project
open_points.question: What does Kernel receive if its room or pointer request id collides with a record belonging to a project outside its granted set?
options: Return only the ordinary not-found refusal and reveal no record
Scope request-id uniqueness and lookup by session or principal
Return the colliding record despite its project
open_points.default_guess: Return the ordinary not-found refusal and never disclose the colliding record.

open_points.subject: A17 configuration validation order
open_points.text: A failed configuration check “names the failed item,” but no order or aggregation rule is declared when several checks fail
open_points.question: When several configuration items are invalid, does startup report all failures or only one, and if only one, which check has precedence?
options: Report every failed item without values
Report the first failure in a declared item order
Report an implementation-selected failure
open_points.default_guess: Report all failed item names in one diagnostic.

open_points.subject: A17 unknown configuration items
open_points.text: “A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start” does not define which surrounding environment or configuration namespace is inspected for unknown items
open_points.question: What counts as an unknown Registry configuration item rather than an unrelated host or process environment variable?
options: Only unknown keys inside a dedicated Registry configuration object or prefix
Any environment variable not listed by A17
Unknown items are ignored
open_points.default_guess: Validate only keys in a dedicated Registry configuration namespace and reject unknown keys there.

open_points.subject: A17 owner-only token test
open_points.text: Rule 1 permits an owner-only start with none of the four service tokens, while required test 1 says “A configuration without Client Portal's token stops the start” without limiting that test to a partial service-token set
open_points.question: Does a configuration with no Client Portal token start when all four tokens are absent?
options: Yes; the test applies only when at least one service token is configured
No; Client Portal's token is always required
Owner-only mode requires an explicit mode flag rather than being inferred from zero tokens
open_points.default_guess: Yes; zero service tokens means owner-only, while any partial set fails.

open_points.subject: A18 backup snapshot instant
open_points.text: A backup “records ... its instant” and is a consistent copy taken while Registry runs, but the instant is not tied to the start, snapshot point, completion or successful check
open_points.question: Which instant is recorded and used for age, restore data-loss claims and comparison with the import instant?
options: The store snapshot's logical instant
The instant writing begins
The instant the backup passes its check
open_points.default_guess: Record the logical instant at which the consistent store snapshot is taken.

open_points.subject: A18 plaintext check file cleanup
open_points.text: Registry decrypts a backup “into a temporary file” and removes it, while a failed backup or deletion leaves no partial file and Registry keeps serving; the rules do not cover failure to remove the decrypted temporary file
open_points.question: What happens if removal of the plaintext temporary file fails?
options: Stop serving until it is securely removed
Keep serving, emit a diagnostic and retry cleanup
Place the temporary file only on an encrypted ephemeral filesystem and treat failed cleanup as a diagnostic
open_points.default_guess: Use an encrypted private temporary area, keep serving, and retry cleanup while reporting the failure.

open_points.subject: A18 continuing integrity of kept backups
open_points.text: Each backup is checked “right after writing,” but the formal invariant says “every kept backup is ... checked” and no rule rechecks corruption or tampering that occurs later
open_points.question: Are existing retained backups revalidated, and when is a backup considered safe to restore after its creation-time check?
options: Revalidate all retained backups at every daily run
Revalidate a selected backup immediately before restoration
Rely permanently on the creation-time check
open_points.default_guess: Revalidate the selected backup immediately before restoration and delete/refuse it if validation fails.

open_points.subject: A18 post-restore reconciliation gate
open_points.text: The owner must bring restored records to the current retention state before enabling tokens, but “Registry ... cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done”
open_points.question: What prevents service tokens from being enabled before the required reconciliation is complete, and what evidence marks completion?
options: Nothing technical; this is solely an owner procedure
Require an explicit durable reconciliation-complete mark before service-enabled startup
Require a separately generated reconciliation manifest that Registry applies and records
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit durable reconciliation-complete mark that is required before a service-enabled start.

open_points.subject: A18 pre-import restore prohibition
open_points.text: “The owner never restores a backup made before the import” is the only mechanism preserving the one-time migration closure across restoration
open_points.question: How is restoration of a pre-import backup prevented or detected?
options: It is only an operational promise by the owner
Registry refuses service-enabled startup when the restored store lacks the closure but retained backup metadata proves an import occurred
Keep the migration closure or an import-completed marker outside the restorable store
open_points.default_guess: Keep an import-completed marker outside the restorable store and refuse a restored store that would remove it.

open_points.subject: A01 publish replay after type removal
open_points.text: A01 requires a repeat to pass the current type check and says a removed type is refused, while R0-88 says a retry is still allowed when the project remains granted and is not archived and then returns the pointer it made
open_points.question: Does a same-request-id publish retry succeed after its artifact type has been removed from the current release?
options: Refuse it as an unknown type
Return the existing pointer because the original publish was accepted
Return it only through a type-independent replay lookup
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing pointer after authorization and project-lifecycle checks, without requiring the type to remain declared.

open_points.subject: M10 backup retention after import
open_points.text: The changed lifecycle says “no backup made before the import is kept once one holding the closure has passed its check,” but A16 says deletion failures are retried later, which leaves such backups kept after the new backup passes
open_points.question: Must successful checking of the post-import backup wait for deletion of every pre-import backup, or may those backups remain temporarily after deletion failure?
options: They may remain temporarily and the lifecycle statement is eventual
The post-import backup run is not complete until every old backup is deleted
A deletion failure stops Registry from serving
open_points.default_guess: Allow temporary retention after deletion failure and state the lifecycle condition as eventual.

open_points.subject: M10 restoration invariant
open_points.text: The changed lifecycle says that no pre-import backup “is ever restored,” but restoration is an owner action outside Registry and A18 says Registry cannot enforce the owner's reconciliation procedure
open_points.question: What mechanism, if any, makes the claim that a pre-import backup is never restored true?
options: It is only an operational owner obligation
An external non-restorable import marker prevents it
Registry detects the missing closure at startup and refuses service-enabled operation
open_points.default_guess: Use an external import-completed marker and refuse service-enabled startup if the restored store lacks its closure.

open_points.subject: M11 replacement of an uploaded file
open_points.text: The changed model says the uploaded file is “replaced by the next upload,” while A16 says “a refused upload — too large or unreadable — replaces nothing”
open_points.question: Does “next upload” mean every upload attempt or only the next successfully accepted upload?
options: Only a successfully accepted upload replaces it
Every upload attempt replaces or clears it
An unreadable upload clears the prior file but an oversized one does not
open_points.default_guess: Only a successfully accepted upload replaces the prior file.
